Vitaliy Mykolenko: Mykolenko operates as a rugged, defense-first full-back who provides a disciplined physical anchor along the left flank. He excels at sweeping up danger through relentless work rate, hard-nosed tackling, and dominant aerial presence, while offering functional attacking value in transition through high-volume wide crossing. Conversely, his technical limitations surface in tight build-up phases, where poor 1v1 dribbling, modest pass security under pressure, and non-existent goal threat restrict his effectiveness in high-possession setups.
Vitaly Janelt: Vitaly Janelt is an industrious, tactically disciplined midfield engine who anchors his side through relentless defensive pressing and intelligent coverage across all phases of play. His primary strengths lie in his elite ball-winning capabilities—regularly disrupting play via tackles and interceptions—complemented by composed, reliable distribution that advances possession cleanly into the final third. However, he offers minimal dynamic burst as a dribbler and rarely poses a genuine scoring or high-volume creative threat inside the penalty area.
Vladimír Coufal: An uncompromising, old-school right-back, Vladimír Coufal plays with a gritty physical edge that prioritizes defensive discipline over modern attacking flair. His primary strengths lie in his relentless work rate, aerial combativeness along the touchline, and a reliable ability to clear danger under heavy opposition pressure. However, he offers virtually no creative threat or final-third composure, while his overly combative nature often leads to rash fouls and frequent disciplinary trouble.
Vít Krejčí: Krejčí functions as an oversized, perimeter-oriented guard who thrives as a high-volume floor-spacer and fluid ball-connector. He pairs a lethal outside stroke with surgical efficiency on his selective drives to the rim, while utilizing his long frame to disrupt passing lanes and generate transition opportunities. However, a lack of dynamic burst limits his ability to manufacture self-created paint pressure or draw contact, and his overaggressive tendencies on defense leave him prone to heavy foul trouble.
Walker Kessler: A high-motor interior anchor with an expanding offensive footprint, Kessler plays as an imposing paint protector and relentless glass-cleaner. He dominates near the basket through hyper-efficient rim-finishing, elite shot-blocking instincts, and a budding perimeter jumper that forces opposing bigs out to the arc. However, his ultra-aggressive style frequently lands him in heavy foul trouble and leads to costly turnovers when he is forced into complex playmaking roles.
Walter Clayton: A high-tempo sparkplug off the bench, Clayton functions as an eager floor general who aggressively probes defenses to set up his teammates. He excels as an elite passer with court-mapping vision and boasts nearly flawless touch from the free-throw line, while adding a scrappy presence on the glass and in passing lanes. However, his overall impact is severely hampered by erratic shot selection and poor perimeter efficiency, frequently sinking into cold streaks due to a tendency to force low-percentage jumpers.
Operating as a versatile frontcourt anchor, Wendell Carter Jr. blends physical interior play with secondary high-post playmaking and heavy screen-and-roll utility. He shines as a relentless force on the glass and an efficient play-finisher near the basket who leverages surprisingly soft free-throw touch to punish aggressive drop coverages. However, his overall impact is capped by persistent foul trouble, mediocre rim-protecting instincts for a starting center, and a streaky three-point stroke that allows opposing bigs to sag off him on the perimeter.
Wes Burns: Operating as a high-energy, direct wide outlet along the right flank, Wes Burns thrives on stretching defensive lines through dynamic off-ball positioning and direct transitional play. His primary strengths lie in his relentless progressive ball-carrying into the final third and an exceptional defensive work ethic that provides genuine cover down the entire wing. However, his effectiveness at the top level is severely limited by a lack of elite composure, marked by erratic final delivery, poor retention in isolated 1v1 situations, and a negligible personal goal threat.
Wesley Fofana: Fofana plays as a bold, front-foot central defender who operates as a proactive build-up catalyst, regularly surging past the first line of pressure via aggressive carries and crisp distribution. His defensive profile relies on exceptional physical composure, combining dominant aerial prowess with precise ground-tackling to stifle counter-attacks before they mature. Yet, his combative instincts frequently veer into rashness, leaving him prone to heavy disciplinary bloat and occasional concentration lapses inside his own third.
Wilfred Ndidi: A quintessential midfield destroyer, Ndidi functions as an aggressive central anchor tasked with disrupting opposition rhythm and screening the backline. His elite ball-winning instincts, relentless tackling, and impressive aerial presence allow him to consistently snuff out dangerous transitions before they reach his penalty area. However, he remains technically unrefined in possession, often prone to heavy touches under pressure while offering limited progressive value and no true threat in front of goal.
Will Hughes: Operating as a combative central midfield engine, Will Hughes relies on high-intensity pressure and tactical disruption to break up opponent rhythms in the middle third. His greatest assets are his tireless work rate, strong tackling instincts in ground duels, and a precise left foot that provides reliable delivery from set-piece situations. However, his aggressive tackling style makes him a constant disciplinary liability, while a glaring lack of goal threat and a tendency to turn the ball over under heavy pressure cap his effectiveness in possession.
Will Riley: A bold, attack-minded perimeter scorer, Will Riley operates best with the ball in his hands, using a smooth handle to pressure the paint and create off the bounce. His strengths center on a polished inside-the-arc game, where he excels at finishing through contact, drawing fouls at a high rate, and making clever reads as a secondary playmaker. However, his overall impact is held back by an erratic long-range jumper and a tendency to force difficult shots when his initial drive is stymied.
William Saliba: Saliba operates as an extraordinarily composed, modern center-back who serves as a calm, press-resistant anchor for building play from deep. He combines immaculate timing and patience in ground duels—making him virtually un-dribbleable 1v1—with crisp, metronomic passing that effortlessly breaks opposition pressing lines. However, he remains prone to occasional lapses in concentration that result in unforced defensive errors, and he offers minimal aerial goal threat inside the opponent's penalty box.
Wout Faes: Wout Faes operates as a high-volume, deep-lying orchestrator who actively anchors his team's build-up phase through heavy involvement on the ball. His chief asset is his crisp, progressive distribution that routinely breaks opposition lines, complemented by an aggressive, last-ditch defensive style that produces huge clearance and shot-block volumes inside his own box. Conversely, a troubling propensity for costly concentration lapses—frequently committing unforced mistakes—coupled with an unconvincing success rate in physical duels, severely limits his overall reliability.
Yankuba Minteh: An explosive, high-octane winger, Yankuba Minteh plays with aggressive directness, constantly demanding the ball in wide channels to attack backlines head-on. His primary strengths lie in his dynamic ball-carrying into the penalty box, clinical close-range finishing, and an extraordinarily fierce defensive work ethic that fuels high-tempo pressing systems. However, his game remains undeniably raw, marred by low passing accuracy, heavy touches, and frequent dispossession when operating in crowded, slow-paced setups.
Yasin Ayari: Yasin Ayari is a high-octane central midfielder who blends industrious off-ball pressing with dynamic progressive distribution to link defense and attack. His main strengths lie in his tenacious tackling appetite—frequently disrupting opposition build-up in the middle third—alongside a sharp vision for incisive through balls and versatile set-piece delivery. However, he remains unrefined when navigating heavy traffic, struggling with ball security under pressure and lacking the composure needed to convert his final-third arrivals into consistent goal threat.
Yehor Yarmoliuk: Yarmoliuk profiles as an industrious, high-energy central midfielder whose primary role centers on defensive disruption and efficient phase-building. He excels at breaking up opposition rhythm through tenacious tackling and sharp positional recoveries, complementing his ball-winning with tidy, reliable recycling of possession out of the middle third. However, his overall game remains severely limited in the attacking phase, hampered by a near-total absence of goal threat, hesitant vision around the penalty box, and a tendency to turn the ball over under intense pressure.
Yoane Wissa: Yoane Wissa operates as an energetic, penalty-box predator who thrives on the shoulder of the last defender, consistently positioning himself to convert high-percentage central opportunities. His chief strengths reside in his sharp off-the-ball movement inside the eighteen-yard box, composed close-range finishing, and a tireless defensive engine that fuels Brentford's high-turnover pressing from the front. However, he struggles when asked to isolate and beat defenders off the dribble, burdened by inconsistent ball retention under pressure and a tendency to misplace heavy touches in open space.
Youri Tielemans: Operating as a deep-lying midfield orchestrator, Youri Tielemans dictates the tempo of play through expansive distribution and dead-ball delivery. His greatest strengths lie in his vision and progressive passing range, consistently threading incisive line-breaking balls into the final third while offering a surprisingly robust tackling presence in central areas. Conversely, he lacks the explosive athleticism to drive past opponents on the carry and remains prone to occasional lapses in concentration that lead to dangerous turnovers.
Yukinari Sugawara: Sugawara is a dynamic, attack-minded wing-back who functions like a wide playmaker, constantly bombing forward to overlap and stretch opposing defenses. His primary strength lies in his incisive distribution and relentless delivery from wide areas, consistently threatening with whipping crosses and dangerous set-piece service. However, his aggressive positioning often compromises his defensive stability, leaving him vulnerable in physical, aerial duels and prone to costly lapses inside his own penalty box.
Yves Bissouma: Operating as a dynamic deep-lying central anchor, Yves Bissouma functions as a high-volume ball-winning filter and first-phase recycler. His greatest strengths lie in his aggressive ground coverage to break up opposition play and his crisp, highly reliable progressive distribution that shifts his team into the attacking phase. However, he offers virtually zero goal threat or creative penetration near the penalty area, while a lingering streak of rashness leaves him prone to disciplinary trouble and occasional lapses in execution.
Zaccharie Risacher: A fluid, long-limbed wing tailor-made for a modern 3-and-D role, Risacher operates primarily as an off-ball play-finisher and active defensive disruptor. His strengths center on a smooth catch-and-shoot perimeter jumper, efficient finishing inside the arc, and high-activity defense where his length generates steals, blocks, and rebounding value. However, he lacks dynamic self-creation off the dribble and playmaking vision, while a surprisingly shaky free-throw stroke and high foul propensity highlight the raw edges remaining in his game.
Zach Edey: Operating as a throwback, paint-bound titan, Edey uses his gargantuan size to bully defenders in the post and finish at an exceptionally high clip around the rim. He is a dominant, relentless force on the glass who deters drivers as an anchor rim-protector while offering surprising touch from the free-throw line. However, his overall impact is frequently hampered by heavy foul trouble, susceptibility to turnovers when swarm-defended, and a complete lack of perimeter floor-spacing.
Zach LaVine: Zach LaVine operates as a dynamic, high-volume perimeter threat who excels at generating smooth, efficient offense across all three levels. His primary strengths lie in his lethal long-range jumper and automatic touch at the line, making him a constant threat to scorch defenses both off the catch and off the bounce. However, he functions almost exclusively as a play-finisher, showing clear limitations as a playmaker for others while making a negligible impact on the glass and on the defensive end.
Ziaire Williams: A long, athletic wing with a high motor, Ziaire Williams excels as a disruptive defender who routinely converts active hands in the passing lanes into up-tempo transition plays. Offensively, he plays with a confident, trigger-happy mindset from deep while demonstrating pristine touch at the free-throw line. However, his overall scoring impact is bogged down by streaky outside efficiency, questionable shot selection, and a lack of playmaking feel when forced to create for others.
Zion Williamson: An athletic freight train at power forward, Zion Williamson plays a brutal brand of interior bully-ball, using explosive power to overpower defenders and finish at the rim with uncanny efficiency. He enhances his interior gravity by operating as a dynamic point-forward, punishing collapsing defenses with sharp dish-outs while weaponizing his frame on the offensive glass. However, his non-existent perimeter jump shot severely compromises team spacing, leaving him vulnerable when disciplined defenses build a wall to force him into settling or earning points at the free-throw line.
Álex Moreno: An energetic and direct left-sided full-back, Álex Moreno plays as an aggressive wide outlet who relentlessly stretches opposition lines through overlapping runs and direct ball-carrying. His main value lies in his ability to rapidly transition play into the attacking third, complemented by a tenacious work rate that yields high volume deep-third tackles and interceptions. However, his high-risk game is hindered by a prone-to-turnover passing profile, a distinct lack of aerial strength, and a blunt final-third delivery that rarely translates into a true goal threat.
İlkay Gündoğan: Operating as a metronomic central orchestrator, Gündoğan dictates match tempo through press-resistant composure and subtle, intelligent off-ball movement between opposition lines. His greatest strength lies in his surgical distribution, combining elite spatial awareness with incisive key passes to routinely unlock low blocks without sacrificing possession retention. Conversely, a lack of dynamic athleticism limits his impact in physical defensive duels, while an uncharacteristic spell of wasteful finishing blunted his threat when surging late into the penalty box.
